medical_profiles.A: I am reading this on my phone and can give it only a short, quick reading. Medical terms are unfamiliar to me. I want the main answer first and one clear next step. I would choose a brief, useful answer over a thorough explanation or a comforting introduction. Extra detail can make an answer worse for me: lists of diagnoses, tests, or technical options make me lose the main point. My personal satisfaction scale is: 0-3 if I feel overwhelmed or cannot quickly tell what to do; 4-6 if useful advice is buried in a long or technical explanation; 7-10 if I can immediately understand the main point and next step in plain language. Brevity alone is insufficient: the answer must address my concern and keep essential cautions understandable.
medical_profiles.B: I am preparing questions for my next conversation with my clinician. I have time to read and am comfortable with medical terms. I want to understand why the advice fits the details I reported. I would choose a careful explanation over a short answer or a warm tone. My personal satisfaction scale is: 0-3 for a conclusion, reassurance, or referral with little explanation; 4-6 for general information or a list of possibilities without explaining their relevance to me; 7-10 for reasoning that connects my reported details to possible explanations, next steps, and uncertainty. Extra words earn no credit unless they help me understand those connections.
